subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw own an opt-in global `turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` policy and process-managed fence/abort lifecycle for all background context-engine plugins, rather than reuse an existing host timeout or require plugin-owned handling?
rationale: This changes durable operator configuration and the ownership boundary between the generic host scheduler and third-party context-engine maintenance; source review can assess mechanics but cannot select the permanent product contract.

options.title: Adopt the opt-in core contract
options.body: Accept the new disabled-by-default setting and host-owned fence/checkpoint lifecycle as the supported way to bound non-cooperative background maintenance.

options.title: Reuse an existing host timeout
options.body: Narrow the design to an already-supported compaction/runtime timeout contract if maintainers want one host policy instead of another public setting.

options.title: Keep timeout ownership with plugins
options.body: Pause this PR and define an SDK/plugin lifecycle contract if timeout selection and cancellation behavior should remain engine-specific.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opt-in core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the new disabled-by-default setting and host-owned fence/checkpoint lifecycle as the supported way to bound non-cooperative background maintenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related proposal directly examined the alternative of using an existing host safety timeout on this same maintenance path.
